concepts.title: Types of Natural Resources
concepts.definition: Natural resources are materials obtained from nature that satisfy human needs. They are classified as renewable (replenish naturally) and non-renewable (finite, cannot be replenished quickly).
concepts.key_idea: Resources are grouped by whether they naturally renew within a human timescale.
question_patterns: classify a given resource as renewable or non-renewable
list examples of renewable and non-renewable resources
distinguish between renewable and non-renewable resources
explain why coal is a non-renewable resource
identify which resources are replenished naturally

solution_steps.explain: Note the name and origin of the resource.
Determine if the resource regenerates within a human lifespan.
If renewable, mark renewable; otherwise mark non-renewable.

worked_examples.question: Classify solar energy and petroleum as renewable or non-renewable.
worked_examples.solution: Solar energy is replenished naturally by the Sun, so it is renewable. Petroleum takes millions of years to form, so it is non-renewable.
worked_examples.answer: Solar energy = renewable; petroleum = non-renewable

worked_examples.question: Is groundwater a renewable or non-renewable resource?
worked_examples.solution: Groundwater is replenished by the water cycle, but overuse can deplete it faster than it recharges. In principle it is renewable.
worked_examples.answer: Renewable (if used sustainably)

concepts.title: Renewable Resources
concepts.definition: Renewable resources are those that can be replenished naturally over a short period of time, such as sunlight, wind, water, and biomass.
concepts.key_idea: Renewable resources flow continuously or regenerate within a human timescale when used sustainably.

solution_steps.action: State the definition of renewable resource
solution_steps.explain: A renewable resource regenerates naturally within a short period.
Check whether the resource is naturally replenished on a human timescale.
If it regenerates naturally in a short time, it is renewable; otherwise it is not.

worked_examples.solution: Wind is caused by atmospheric processes driven by the Sun and is continuously available, so it regenerates naturally.
worked_examples.answer: Wind is renewable because it is naturally and continuously replenished.

concepts.title: Non-Renewable Resources
concepts.definition: Non-renewable resources are those that exist in fixed quantities and cannot be replenished once used, such as coal, petroleum, and natural gas.
concepts.key_idea: Non-renewable resources form over geological time and are exhausted with use.
question_patterns: classify a resource as non-renewable with reasons
explain why petroleum is non-renewable
list examples of non-renewable resources
compare renewable and non-renewable resources
justify why minerals are non-renewable

solution_steps.action: State the definition of non-renewable resource
solution_steps.explain: A non-renewable resource exists in limited stock and does not regenerate on a human timescale.
Check whether the resource forms over millions of years and is finite in quantity.
If it is finite and forms over geological time, it is non-renewable.

worked_examples.question: Why is coal classified as a non-renewable resource?
worked_examples.solution: Coal forms from buried plant matter over millions of years and exists in limited quantities, so it cannot be replenished quickly.
worked_examples.answer: Coal is non-renewable because it forms over geological time and is finite.

worked_examples.question: Explain another aspect of Non-Renewable Resources.
worked_examples.solution: Non-renewable resources form over geological time and are exhausted with use.
worked_examples.answer: Non-renewable resources form over geological time and are exhausted with use.

concepts.title: Forests and Their Conservation
concepts.definition: Forests are large areas covered chiefly with trees that provide timber, fuel, fodder, and maintain ecological balance. Conservation means using forests wisely and replanting to ensure their continued availability.
concepts.key_idea: Forests are renewable only if the rate of use does not exceed the rate of regeneration.
question_patterns: explain the importance of forests
list methods of forest conservation
describe the effects of deforestation
justify why afforestation is necessary
compare conservation and preservation of forests

solution_steps.explain: Note whether the question concerns use, loss, or conservation of forests.
Use rate of use <= rate of regeneration to decide sustainability.
Suggest afforestation, reduced felling, or protected areas as needed.

worked_examples.question: A forest is being felled at 200 hectares per year but regenerates at 80 hectares per year. Is this sustainable?
worked_examples.solution: Since 200 > 80, the rate of use exceeds regeneration, so it is not sustainable.
worked_examples.answer: Not sustainable; afforestation and reduced felling are needed.

worked_examples.question: List three methods of forest conservation.
worked_examples.solution: Afforestation, controlled grazing, and declaring protected areas conserve forests.
worked_examples.answer: Afforestation, controlled grazing, protected areas

concepts.title: Water Resources
concepts.definition: Water resources include all forms of water available for human use -- surface water (rivers, lakes), groundwater, and rainwater. Fresh water is a small fraction of total water on Earth.
concepts.key_idea: Only about 3% of Earth's water is fresh, and much of it is locked in ice; hence water must be conserved.
question_patterns: calculate the percentage of fresh water on Earth
list sources of surface water
explain the need for water conservation
describe methods of rainwater harvesting
compare surface water and groundwater

solution_steps.explain: Note whether the question concerns surface, ground, or rain water.
Use fresh_water_fraction = fresh_water / total_water if computing a ratio.
State whether the resource is abundant or scarce and suggest conservation.

worked_examples.question: If fresh water is about 3% of total water on Earth, express this as a fraction and a decimal.
Of the 3% fresh water, about 2% is locked in ice. What fraction of total water is available as liquid fresh water?
worked_examples.solution: Available fresh water = 3% - 2% = 1% = 0.01 of total water.

concepts.title: Mineral Resources
concepts.definition: Mineral resources are naturally occurring substances obtained from the Earth's crust, such as iron ore, copper, bauxite, and limestone. They are non-renewable and formed over millions of years.
concepts.key_idea: Minerals are finite and non-renewable, so they must be used judiciously and recycled where possible.
question_patterns: classify minerals as metallic or non-metallic
list uses of common minerals
explain why minerals are non-renewable
describe methods of mineral conservation
identify minerals used in daily life

solution_steps.explain: Note the mineral name and its type.
Determine if the mineral is metallic or non-metallic.
List uses and suggest recycling or reduced use.

worked_examples.question: Classify iron ore, bauxite, and limestone as metallic or non-metallic.
worked_examples.solution: Iron ore and bauxite yield metals (iron and aluminium), so they are metallic. Limestone does not yield a metal, so it is non-metallic.
worked_examples.answer: Iron ore = metallic, bauxite = metallic, limestone = non-metallic

worked_examples.answer: Electrical wiring and alloys

concepts.title: Land Resources and Soil
concepts.definition: Land resources include the soil and terrain used for agriculture, forestry, and settlement. Soil is the upper layer of land that supports plant growth and is formed slowly by weathering of rocks.
concepts.key_idea: Soil forms very slowly, so erosion must be controlled to keep land productive.

solution_steps.explain: Note whether the question concerns erosion, fertility, or conservation.

worked_examples.answer: Terrace farming and contour ploughing

concepts.title: Conventional Energy Resources
concepts.definition: Conventional energy resources are traditional sources such as coal, petroleum, natural gas, and hydropower that have been used for a long time. Most are non-renewable except hydropower.
concepts.key_idea: Conventional sources are widely used but most are finite and polluting.
question_patterns: list conventional sources of energy

solution_steps.explain: Note the source name.

worked_examples.question: Classify coal, petroleum, and hydropower as renewable or non-renewable.
worked_examples.solution: Coal and petroleum form over millions of years, so they are non-renewable. Hydropower relies on the water cycle, so it is renewable.
worked_examples.answer: Coal = non-renewable, petroleum = non-renewable, hydropower = renewable

concepts.title: Non-Conventional Energy Resources
concepts.definition: Non-conventional energy resources are renewable and cleaner alternatives such as solar energy, wind energy, biogas, and tidal energy that have been developed more recently.
concepts.key_idea: Non-conventional sources are renewable and cause less pollution, making them sustainable long-term options.

concepts.title: Sustainable Development and Conservation of Resources
concepts.definition: Sustainable development means using resources at a rate that meets present needs without compromising the ability of future generations to meet their needs. Conservation is the careful and planned use of resources to prevent depletion.
concepts.key_idea: Resources must be used so that they last for future generations; the three R's -- reduce, reuse, recycle -- guide conservation.
question_patterns: define sustainable development
explain the three R's of conservation
justify the need for resource conservation
describe how individuals can conserve resources

solution_steps.action: Identify the resource and its use
solution_steps.explain: Note the resource and how it is being used.
Check if use_rate <= regeneration_rate.
If not sustainable, suggest reduce, reuse, recycle or alternative resources.

worked_examples.question: A groundwater source is used at 150 units per year but recharges at 100 units per year. Is this use sustainable?
worked_examples.solution: Since 150 > 100, use exceeds recharge, so it is not sustainable.
worked_examples.answer: Not sustainable; reduce use to at most 100 units per year.

worked_examples.question: State the three R's of conservation and give one example of each.
worked_examples.solution: Reduce (use less water), reuse (use shopping bags again), recycle (recycle paper into new paper).
worked_examples.answer: Reduce, reuse, recycle
